title: Page header
summary: The top of a page, a section or a record: a breadcrumb row, a title bar with actions, and a note line. Without an explicit heading, the crumbs, chips and actions collapse onto a single row by default; spacious opts back into the multi-row breakdown. Stacks by its own width, with the actions full width and touch-sized on a phone.

props.name: heading
props.description: The title. Without it (and without default or actions content) the title bar is not shown.

props.name: level
props.description: The heading level the title exposes to assistive technology (aria-level).

props.name: variant
props.description: page is the standard page top; section is a titled section inside a page; record is the compact strip of a single-record page (chips left, actions right; on a narrow container the chips move to a row below).

props.name: spacious
props.description: Without a heading the crumbs, chips and actions share one row. Set spacious for the multi-row breakdown (crumbs, then a title bar with actions, then the note line), for a long title or many badges. No effect when heading is set.

props.name: sticky
props.description: Pins the header to the top of the scrolling page body while the content scrolls: in pk-app-shell flush under the app bar (the body is the scroller), in a plain page at the top of the viewport. It is its own stacking context one above in-body sticky strips, so a popover opened from the header draws over them.

props.name: stickyFrom
props.description: With sticky, the width above which the header stays pinned: always, phone (above the phone breakpoint) or tablet. At and below it the header scrolls away, leaving room above the on-screen keyboard. The opposite sense of tabs-from.

props.name: crumbs
props.description: The breadcrumb trail as a JSON array of { "label", "href" }, drawn in a pk-breadcrumb above the title (the last crumb is the current page: aria-current, and the page title when no heading is set). An href that is not a same-site path, http(s), mailto, tel or sms address draws a crumb without a link. Use it instead of the breadcrumb slot, not with it.

props.name: actionsOverflow
props.description: Collapses the actions slot into one icon button that opens a menu at the named width and below (phone, tablet) or always. Each slotted action becomes a menu item with its label, icon-name, disabled and danger state; choosing one clicks the original, so its handlers, href and events are unchanged, and the title bar stays one row high. Use pk-button or link actions as direct children of the slot; a pk-dropdown or pk-card-menu among them is flattened into its own items (headers kept, selecting one selects the original).

props.name: overflowLabel
props.description: The accessible name of the overflow button drawn by actionsOverflow.

props.name: breadcrumbLabel
props.description: The accessible name of the breadcrumb landmark drawn from crumbs.

props.name: homeHref
props.description: An address for a leading home crumb: an icon-only link (named by homeLabel) first in the trail crumbs draws. Empty draws none.

props.name: homeLabel
props.description: The accessible name of the home crumb.

props.name: homeIcon
props.description: The icon of the home crumb (a name of the icon sprite).

props.name: tabsFrom
props.description: Where the docked tabs strip shows: always, or only at phone or tablet width and below (above it the strip is hidden, so a page that shows every section at that width needs no strip).

props.name: tabs
props.description: The docked strip as data: an array of { value, label, count?, visible? }, the same shape as pk-record-form. The element draws a pk-tabs at the foot of the header (a pk-tabs in the tabs slot wins); count is the badge after the label and a tab with visible false is left out. With sticky the strip stays in view with the bar. Listen for pk-tab-change for the chosen value.

props.name: backLink
props.description: Draws a back link above the header to the last crumb before the current one that has a usable href: a ghost icon-only button with a chevron, named "Back to <label>". On a header of 30rem or less with no heading (the crumbs are the title) the chevron takes the start of row one and the home and parent crumbs fold away, so the title shares the row with the actions. Off by default because the app shell can draw its own.

slots.name: title
slots.description: A real heading element for the title (a pk-heading) in place of the built-in title text; set heading too so the title bar is drawn. The page shell (showTitleBar, so every built-in page type) slots a pk-heading level 1 here.
Beside the title: status chips, badges or your own heading element. In the record variant on a narrow container they drop to their own row under the title and actions.

slots.name: breadcrumb
slots.description: A pk-breadcrumb (or any trail) above the title; hidden when empty.

slots.name: actions
slots.description: Buttons at the right of the title bar; full width and touch-sized on a narrow container. Give each an icon-name and collapse="phone" so it folds to the icon alone on a phone (its text stays the accessible name).

slots.name: meta
slots.description: A note or metadata line under the title bar; hidden when empty.

slots.name: tabs
slots.description: A tab strip (pk-tabs with tabs only, or your own) docked at the foot of the header, so with sticky it stays in view with the bar; replaces the strip drawn from the tabs array; hidden when empty or when tabs-from says it does not apply at this width.

events.name: pk-tab-change
events.description: The docked strip chose a tab.

parts.name: overflow-button
parts.description: The icon button that opens the overflow menu.

parts.name: back
parts.description: The back link drawn when backLink is set.

parts.name: titlebar
parts.description: The row holding the title and the actions.

parts.name: lead
parts.description: The title and the default slot.

parts.name: title
parts.description: The built-in title text (hidden when the title slot is filled).

parts.name: strip
parts.description: The pk-tabs the element draws from the tabs array (the tabs slot's fallback).

parts.name: chips
parts.description: Wraps the default slot; a plain pass-through except in a narrow record, where it is its own row.

cssProperties.name: --pk-page-header-title-size
cssProperties.description: Title font size (the built-in title text; a slotted pk-heading takes its own variant).

cssProperties.name: --pk-page-header-sticky-top
cssProperties.description: Offset from the top of the scroller when sticky. 0 is flush under the app bar inside pk-app-shell; on a plain page under a fixed bar of your own set it to that bar's height (for example var(--app-header-h)).

a11y: The header is a header element, not a banner landmark, so it is safe inside main. With a slotted title (the page shell uses a pk-heading level 1, focusable with tabindex -1 so a route change can move focus to it) the title is that element's own real heading and the built-in text is hidden. Otherwise the title is exposed as a heading whose level you choose with level, so it fits the page outline (use 1 for a page, 2 or 3 for a section). Give the breadcrumb slot a pk-breadcrumb, which is its own labelled navigation landmark; a home crumb is an icon-only link first in that trail and needs an aria-label. Tabs in the tabs slot keep their own tablist semantics. Any variant with no heading attribute renders single-row by default (unless spacious is set), with the last breadcrumb crumb (already aria-current="page") standing in for the title; pk-page-header does not own pk-breadcrumb's slotted content, so it cannot add a heading role to that crumb for you — add role="heading" and the matching aria-level (matching level) on that last crumb yourself, as in the record example below.

examples.title: Sticky only from a width up
examples.html:
<pk-page-header heading="Phone and up" level="2" sticky sticky-from="phone"></pk-page-header>
<pk-page-header heading="Tablet and up" level="2" sticky sticky-from="tablet"></pk-page-header>
